related_questions.question: What is the new law on retirement?

text_blocks.snippet: The SECURE 2.0 Act, passed in late 2022, continues to roll out significant changes to retirement regulations, impacting areas like required minimum distributions (RMDs), catch-up contributions, and automatic enrollment in 401(k) plans. Additionally, the Social Security Fairness Act, enacted in early 2025, addresses the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and Government Pension Offset (GPO) for certain workers.
Here's a breakdown of key changes:

list.title: Increased RMD Age:
list.snippet: The age at which individuals must begin taking RMDs from retirement accounts has been raised to 73, and will further increase to 75 in 2033.

list.title: Catch-Up Contributions:
list.snippet: For those aged 60-63, catch-up contributions to 401(k) and SIMPLE IRA plans will increase to $11,250 starting in 2025.

list.title: Automatic Enrollment in 401(k)s:
list.snippet: New 401(k) plans established after December 29, 2022, must automatically enroll new employees at a 3-10% contribution rate, with automatic increases in subsequent years.

list.title: Roth Matching Contributions:
list.snippet: Employers can now allow employees to choose whether employer matching contributions are treated as pre-tax or Roth (after-tax) contributions.

list.title: Emergency Withdrawals:
list.snippet: SECURE 2.0 allows for penalty-free withdrawals of up to $1,000 from retirement accounts for certain emergency expenses, once per year.

list.title: Long-Term Part-Time Employees:
list.snippet: The law expands eligibility for retirement plan participation for long-term, part-time employees, requiring them to be included after 500 hours of service for two consecutive years.

list.title: Saver's Match:
list.snippet: A new Saver's Match program is being established to incentivize retirement savings.

list.title: WEP and GPO Elimination:
list.snippet: This act eliminates the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and Government Pension Offset (GPO), which previously reduced or eliminated Social Security benefits for those with pensions based on non-covered work.

list.title: Increased Benefits:
list.snippet: This change will lead to increased Social Security benefits for certain workers, such as teachers, firefighters, police officers, and federal employees covered by the Civil Service Retirement System.
401(k) Contribution Limit: The annual contribution limit for 401(k) plans has increased to $23,500 for 2025.
IRA Contribution Limit: The annual contribution limit for IRAs remains at $7,000.
CalSavers: California continues to operate its CalSavers retirement savings program for workers without access to employer-sponsored plans.

related_questions.question: What are the big changes coming for retirement savings?
related_questions.snippet: Contribution limits are going up for people with workplace retirement plans. In 2025, those ages 50-plus can put up to $31,000 into a 401(k), 403(b) or Thrift Savings Plan (and most 457 plans). That's $500 above the 2024 cap. The limit for workers 49 and younger ticks up from $23,000 to $23,500 in 2025.

related_questions.question: What are the new retirement rules for 2025?
related_questions.snippet: A new catch-up rule allows employees age 60 to 63 to contribute up to $34,750 to their 401(k) starting in 2025. Automatic enrollment now will be required for most new 401(k) and 403(b) plans starting in 2025. Part-time workers are now eligible to join retirement plans after two consecutive years with 500+ hours.
